notes: Apple's 5 V 1 A iPhone adapter, label A1265 (100-240 V input), as opened in Ken Shirriff's 2012 teardown. The later A1385 is a different model with a different controller and a single optocoupler, so check the model number printed on your unit.

gaps: The article's text gives no value for the two large input electrolytic capacitors; footnote 14's price table lists a 3.3 uF 400 V electrolytic but the text does not tie it to them, so no value is claimed.
The output POSCAP marked '330 j90' is 300 mF in footnote 13 and 330 uF in footnote 14's price table (a misprint is likely, not settled here), so only its marking and 6.3 V are claimed.

The author calls every identification tentative (footnote 13); for the controller he says the chip could be something else but the circuit matches the L6565 (footnote 7). The text spells the maker STMicrosystems; EB936 may be a date code.
The article gives the DC bus as 125-340 V in the text and 145-345 V in footnote 1; neither is claimed as a part rating.

No count is stated for the 1HNK60 transistors, the PS2801-1 optocouplers or the TL431 (footnote 11 adds a second optocoupler and a second 431 regulator in the protection circuit), so none is set; the fusible resistor has only its 10 ohm value.
The model number A1265 appears in the text of the label photo and in a reader comment, not in the article's prose.
No production years are given; the post is from May 2012 (URL path, first reader comment dated 19 May 2012).
The L6565DTR page on LCSC is titled for the DTR ordering code; the article names the chip only as L6565, and the datasheet itself could not be read as text.
method: Ken Shirriff, 'Apple iPhone charger teardown: quality in a tiny expensive package' (righto.com, May 2012), read as text with footnotes 1, 7, 11, 13 and 14; photos not read.
Patent Refinery's Apple A1385 5W USB charger teardown page, used only for the note that the A1385 has a different controller and one optocoupler.

LCSC datasheet link for L6565DTR (C9381): the page opens, no bot check, and its title names the part, but it is not a readable PDF; the LCSC product page C9381 also names L6565DTR. No field rests on either.

comps.spec: USB output 5 V 1 A. Label caption reads 'Model No A1265', input 100-240 V 50/60 Hz 0.15 A, output 5V 1A.
L6565 8-pin quasi-resonant SMPS controller, the author's identification from the circuit (the text writes the maker as STMicrosystems); the chip is marked FLEX01 and EB936
Striped fusible resistor, 10 ohm, on the input before the bridge rectifier
Four input rectifier diodes marked 1JLGE9, identified as 1J 600 V 1 A; footnote 13 says the JS4 package holds two diodes
Two large black electrolytic capacitors with white print and a stripe, smoothing the rectified input together with the inductor

Flyback transformer (yellow in the photos) with an EQ-style ferrite core, each core half about 6 x 11 x 4 mm, 0.28 mm air gap; three windings: high-voltage primary, low-voltage auxiliary and high-current low-voltage output

PS2801-1 optocouplers (footnote 13), carrying the output-voltage feedback across the isolation gap; footnote 11 describes a second optocoupler in the over-temperature and over-voltage shutdown circuit
SCD34 Schottky output rectifier, 3 A 40 V (footnote 13)
USB connector (the silver rectangle in the photos) through which the secondary board feeds the output
Switching transistors marked 1HNK60, identified as 600 V 1 A N-channel MOSFETs (footnote 13); the article describes a main switching transistor and a second one in the clamp circuit
Blue Y capacitor between the primary and secondary sides, marked 'MC B221K X1 400V Y1 250V', 220 pF
Sanyo POSCAP tantalum polymer capacitor marked '330 j90', 6.3 V (the 'j' marks the voltage, '90' a date code)
TL431 regulator in the secondary feedback circuit that monitors the output voltage
